extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants, and USPTO examiners (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for preparing, filing, and processing amendments (claims, drawings, specification) in U.S. patent applications, including handling of non-compliant and preliminary amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the claims in each amendment paper must be presented in ascending numerical order. Consecutive canceled or not entered claims may be aggregated into one statement (e.g., Claims 1–5 (canceled)). The original numbering of the claims must be preserved throughout prosecution; when claims are canceled, the remaining claims must not be renumbered. New claims must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example listing provided (Claims 1-5 (canceled), Claim 6 (withdrawn), Claim 7 (previously presented), etc.). A canceled claim can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled claims/matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim cancelled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amending a replacement paragraph or section, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled. Present a marked-up version using underlining to indicate added subject matter and strike-through to indicate deleted subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable alternative status identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent delays, the Office will waive certain provisions of 37 CFR 1.121 and accept alternative status identifiers not specifically set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(c) if the amendment otherwise complies with 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping examples: 'Original' → 'Original Claim' / 'Originally Filed Claim'; 'Currently amended' → 'Presently amended' / 'Currently amended claim'; 'Canceled' → 'Canceled without prejudice', 'Cancel', 'Canceled herein', 'Deleted', etc.; 'Withdrawn' → 'Withdrawn from consideration', 'Withdrawn – new', etc.; 'Previously presented' → 'Previously amended', 'Previously added', etc.; 'New' → 'Newly added', 'New claim'; 'Not entered' → 'Not entered claim'. The Office may accept additional variations if the status is accurate and clear; when accepted the examiner is not required to correct the identifiers or notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment compliance and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to an application drawing must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and must be submitted on a replacement sheet of drawings, even when applicant is only submitting better quality drawings without substantive changes. Any additional new drawings must be submitted on a new sheet of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement or new sheets must be attachments to the amendment document and identified in the top margin as 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet.' The replacement sheet must include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet even if only one figure is amended. The figure should not be labeled 'amended.' No proposed drawing corrections in red ink should be submitted; proposed drawing corrections will be treated as non-compliant under 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up drawing copies and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, may be included and must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up copy must be provided when required by the examiner. An explanation of the changes must be presented in the 'Amendments to the Drawings' or the remarks section. If changes to drawing figures are not approved by the examiner, applicant will be notified in the next Office action and must amend the brief and detailed description of drawings if inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of proposed drawing correction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed drawing correction practice has been eliminated. For any changes to the drawings, applicant is required to submit a replacement sheet of drawings with the changes made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter to the official draftsman is no longer required. In response to drawing objections, submit replacement or new sheets with the corrections made. Drawing submissions without any amendments to the specification and claims after allowance should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments (37 CFR 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may make amendments to the specification, including the claims, by examiner's amendments without paragraph/section/claim replacement to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time. Additions or deletions may be made by instructions to make the change at a precise location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendments do not need to comply with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), or (c) of 37 CFR 1.121. If a non-compliant amendment would otherwise place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the non-compliant amendment and correct the non-compliance via an examiner's amendment (e.g., incorrect status identifier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and authorization for examiner's amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's amendment should include the reason why the amendment is non-compliant and indicate how it was corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization from the applicant or attorney/agent of record and extensions of time are not required if the changes are not substantive (e.g., corrections of format errors or typographical errors). Authorization and appropriate extensions are required if the changes made in the examiner's amendment are substantive (e.g., cancellation of a claim or change in scope of claims); such authorization must be given within the time period for reply set forth in the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: General handling of non-compliant amendments (Form PTOL-324)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify applicant by a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment (Form PTOL-324) identifying: (1) which section is non-compliant; (2) items required for compliance; and (3) the reasons why the section is non-compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The type of amendment determines whether applicant is given time to comply and whether the reply must include the corrected section or the entire corrected amendment. The notice will identify required corrections (e.g., a compliant claim listing) and the applicable time period or consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment: preliminary amendment filed after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment filed after the filing date fails to comply, the Technical Support Staff (TSS) will send a notice setting a reply period of 30 days or one month, whichever is later. No extensions permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit a timely reply will result in the application being examined without entry of the preliminary amendment. Applicant's reply must include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment: preliminary amendment present on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment that is present on the filing date fails to comply, the Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE) will send a notice setting a two-month time period for reply. Extensions are available under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply will result in abandonment. Applicant's reply must include either a substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125 (if amendment to the specification) or a complete claim listing under 37 CFR 1.121(c) (if amendment to the claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment: non-final amendment including RCE and similar
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-final amendment including an amendment filed as a submission for an RCE, the TSS will send a notice setting a 30-day or one-month reply period, whichever is later. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply will result in abandonment. Applicant's reply must include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment: after-final amendments and supplemental amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An after-final amendment will be forwarded in unentered status to the examiner. The examiner should indicate non-compliance in the advisory action and attach a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment; the notice provides no new time period. A supplemental amendment filed when there is no suspension of action is not entered as a matter of right and the examiner will notify applicant if not approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For supplemental amendments filed within a suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103, TSS will set a 30-day or one-month reply period with no extensions; failure to reply -> examined without entry. For after-allowance amendments under 37 CFR 1.312, amendments are not entered as a matter of right; examiner may attach Notice (PTO-271); no new time period; any further after-allowance amendment must be submitted before payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendments (including after-final amendments) that add new claims in excess of the number of claims previously paid for in an application must be accompanied by payment of the required excess claims fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay the excess claims fees will result in non-entry of the amendment. See MPEP § 607 for fee details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective directions for entry of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Directions for the entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccuracy in the paragraph number and/or page and line designated, or lack of precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correct place of entry is clear from context, the amendatory paper will be properly amended in the Technology Center, notation will be made and initialed by the examiner, who assumes responsibility for the change. In the next Office action, the applicant should be informed of the alteration and entry. If defective directions and context leave doubt, the applicant will be informed of the nonentry of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application must be signed by a person having authority to prosecute the application. Permitted signatories include: (1) a registered patent attorney or patent agent of record appointed in compliance with § 1.32(b); (2) a registered attorney or agent not of record acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34; (3) an assignee as provided under § 3.71(b); or (4) all of the applicants (§ 1.41(b)) unless an assignee of entire interest has acted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment will not be entered. It will be listed in the contents of the application file but not entered. The examiner will notify applicant and advise to furnish a duplicate properly signed amendment or to ratify the amendment. In a non-final application, applicant should be given a one-month time period (37 CFR 1.135(c)) to ratify. An amendment signed by a person removed from the register under 37 CFR 10.11 is not entered and is submitted to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments signed by applicant when attorney of record exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment signed by the applicant is received in an application in which there is a duly appointed attorney or agent, the amendment should be entered and acted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention should be called to 37 CFR 1.33(a) (patent applications) and 1.33(c) (reexamination proceedings). Two copies of the action should be prepared: one sent to the attorney and the other directly to the applicant. The notation 'Copy to applicant' should appear on the original and both copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is received on or before the mail date of the first Office action (37 CFR 1.115). Any preliminary amendment, regardless of when filed, must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., include a complete listing of all claims and each section begin on a separate sheet). Preliminary amendments in a transmittal letter will not comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a preliminary amendment fails to comply, applicant will be notified and given a non-extendable one-month period to correct (or two months if present on filing date per OIPE practice). Filing preliminary amendments is generally not recommended because changes may not be reflected in the patent application publication if not entered before technical preparations for publication. Applicants are encouraged to incorporate desired amendments into the specification at filing instead of using preliminary amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments present on the filing date: original disclosure and oath/declaration implications
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept 21, 2004, a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure. For earlier filings, it is part of the original disclosure only if referred to in the first executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a preliminary amendment present on filing date contains subject matter not otherwise included in the specification or drawings and the oath/declaration does not refer to it, the Office will not screen for new matter; it is the applicant's obligation to ensure no new matter. If new matter is present, applicant must file a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 referring to the preliminary amendment or cancel the unsupported subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and disapproval of preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment may be disapproved (not entered) if it seeks cancellation of all claims without presenting new/substitute claims, or if it unduly interferes with preparation of a first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors for disapproval include (i) the state of preparation of the first Office action at date of receipt; and (ii) the nature of changes to the specification or claims that would result. Entry of a preliminary amendment will not be disapproved if filed no later than: (i) three months from the filing date for an application under § 1.53(b); (ii) the filing date of a continued prosecution application under § 1.53(d); or (iii) three months from national stage entry under § 1.491. These time periods are not extendable. If filed after these periods, disapproval may be denied subject to supervisory patent examiner approval, and the two-factor test above will be applied.
